summary: TEMPLATE: what the charity does, the causal chain to the tonnes, the year modelled, the bottom line in years of healthy life per $1,000 (quote it live in the write-up), and the biggest uncertainty.

source.title: charityevals' estimate: climate policy and research

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Air pollution these tonnes carry
sections.explainer: Every tonne avoids its heat deaths; a tonne from burning less fossil fuel near people also avoids air-pollution deaths. These rows say how much of the shared air-pollution rate applies to this charity's tonnes (docs/normalization.md 2.5); the rates themselves stay shared.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Spending on the modelled program(s) in the year modelled
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: program expenses, in US dollars, for the activities modelled below and the same year as the reach numbers (say the year in the label and the summary). Cite the audited statement of functional expenses (or the annual report) and the page. Other currencies: a row in local currency times @fx.usd_per_<cur>_<year> (the IRS yearly average, else the World Bank's; add the fact with scripts/link-fx.py), never a typed rate.

rows.explainer: Spreads management and fundraising over programs in proportion to their cost, as GiveWell and ACE do.

source.title: TEMPLATE: regulatory impact assessment / modelling study

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: emissions avoided per year once the rule, law or technology the charity works on is in effect, from the regulator's or a modelling study's estimate (cited), in tonnes of CO₂e.

rows.label: Probability the change happens because of this work
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the probability that the change happens in the period because of the charity's work, from a reference class (similar rules won, similar campaigns) named here. One chance (one bill, one case, one research bet): tag the row `single_event: true`; a share across many grants or campaigns: no tag (normalization.md 2.18).

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (docs/normalization.md 2.9).

rows.label: Years from the grant until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the wait until the tonnes are avoided (the rule's effective date, plants re-powered, trees grown), from the policy's own dates where it has them; discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate; the unit's conversion then discounts the heat deaths from the year the tonne is avoided, so nothing is discounted twice.

rows.label: Discounted years of impact
Expected tonnes averted (before adjustments)
Share of these tonnes from burning less fossil fuel near people
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the tonnes that come from burning less fuel (power, industry, transport) rather than land use, capture or methane. 0 for tonnes with no smoke.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths per tonne of this fuel, relative to the fossil-fuel average
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: this fuel's and place's smoke per tonne of CO₂ against the average behind the shared rate, from per-fuel evidence (deaths per TWh, e.g. Markandya & Wilkinson 2007), not the world average.

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: Read by the tco2e unit's conversion (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly (none here)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: deaths a source counts directly beside the tonnes (a coal plant's own death count), per tonne brought forward, as an input with its source; 0 when the smoke is in air_pollution_weight, so nothing is counted twice.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes that are methane
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the tonnes (CO₂e) that is methane, weighted by tonnes a year before waits and years counted (a conversion row reads no shared assumption); the shared conversion values it by methane's own timing and adds its ozone deaths (docs/normalization.md 2.5). 0 for CO₂ only.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how far the effect size above should be trusted for this charity's setting: publication bias, self-report bias, replication, differences between study populations and this program. A multiplier (1 = take the studies at face value), the product of its parts; say each part, its anchor (the same adjustment in another model of this intervention) and the range.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the outcome that would not have happened without the program (other providers, existing trends, government). Cite coverage data or trend data where possible.

rows.label: This charity's share among those who worked for the result
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: this charity's share among those who campaigned, advised or researched alongside it for the same result (coalition partners, co-authors, other funders of the same work), by everyone's spending and staff time on it. Whoever adopts or carries out the result (the government that legislates and enforces, the company that complies, the lab, funder or health system that uses the research) is never in this denominator: the mobiliser's share below covers them. 1 when it worked alone.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24). For a branch of the charity's own services, grants or purchases, drop mobiliser_share from the formula and set "credit": "delivery".

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12). Keep $missing_data_discount when this branch's outcome rests on the research literature or on judgment rather than on this charity's own data: reach that is a judgment (spending over an assumed cost per person, no count of its own), an effect that is a judgment, or a programme with no outcome data built from the literature on its kind of work. Set the formula to 1 only when the charity's own count of who got the intervention meets an effect measured with a credible counterfactual (its own controlled evaluation, or trials of the same intervention delivered the same way, dose and population), and say which here.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Public money a year that buys the tonnes or funds the work (none here)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: public money the win spends a year once in effect (a tax credit per tonne × the tonnes, grants, public procurement, a won fund's levies) from a shared fact (facts/climate.json: the credit per tonne, the law's yearly cost), as an input with its source; 0 when the tonnes come with no public money.

rows.label: Value lost per dollar of that money, units of value
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: what a dollar of public money costs its payers (docs/normalization.md 2.23): the shared cost of raising it over the payers' consumption on the survey scale (2.14), here US federal taxpayers. Other payers: their country's survey-scale consumption; a levy on traded goods: its payers at the shared compliance-cost multiple, without the cost of raising public funds.

rows.label: What the public money costs its payers, units of value (negative)
rows.explainer: Netted against the tonnes it buys (docs/normalization.md 2.23), over the same years, wait and adjustments as the tonnes, the mobiliser's share included (it is in total_adj: the share applies to the tonnes net of this cost, 2.24): money paid per unit delivered takes every adjustment; a fixed sum (grants, appropriations) all but the evidence step (divide total_adj by evidence_adj); a levy the steps of the spending it pays for.

rows.label: The public money's cost to its payers, in tonnes of CO₂e (negative)
rows.formula: public_cost_uov / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)
rows.explainer: Units of value into tonnes by the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6). Fixed.
